correctness.rationale: For every distinct nonzero basis-image, separation four forces a parity row of weight >=3; any two different images force mutual Hamming distance >=2. Matching along one hypercube coordinate partitions 2^r vectors into adjacent pairs and leaves r pairs unusable, giving the exact upper capacity 2^(r-1)-r. All odd-weight parity rows of weight >=3 attain that capacity. Detailed verification of input weights one, two, three and >=4 proves separation for arbitrary zero and repeated images. The embedded executable exhaustively independently checks 84 small functions and all differences of four complete projective instances, with VERIFY_OK. No finite test is used in place of the all-rank proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural parameter classification for the entire binary subclass at the first unsolved distance-four threshold, rather than a special-case recomputation. Unlike classical identity-function distance-four coding bounds, it handles every kernel and any multiplicities of distinguished-basis images; the exact dependence on their number gives optimal parity overhead for protecting only a linear function. The matching/odd-label mechanism is structural and constructive, and the original 2026 source explicitly identifies the d=4 systematic problem as open.
